currentCard.explanation: IngramSpark описывает матовую фактуру как мягкую на ощупь и не дающую бликов. Глянцевая фактура, напротив, гладкая и блестящая; тканеподобное покрытие и кейс-ламинат относятся к другим вариантам оформления.

literal.prompt: Какое покрытие обложки в списке IngramSpark описано как не дающее бликов?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: IngramSpark Book Textures explicitly labels Matte Cover «Soft feel, no glare, polished», contrasting Gloss «High shine, smooth finish». Therefore the source-attributed non-glare label uniquely selects matte among the listed named products. Cloth/jacketed case describe other formats; actual finish options may combine, but the stem narrowly asks the list description, not a universal exclusivity.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Она мягкая на ощупь и не бликует; IngramSpark также отмечает её полированную поверхность.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Soft feel/no glare are explicit. However the source’s bare marketing adjective «polished» does not establish that a matte cover has a physically «полированную поверхность»: the note adds an unqualified physical-surface reading. A refined/finished appearance is also an ordinary sense of polished here. The claimed polished surface therefore lacks clear primary support in the retained context.

absoluteLevel.ground: Matte versus gloss glare is broad adult consumer vocabulary. The original soft-versus-hard cover naming shortcut is gone. The company attribution does not make this commonplace finish property thematic/expert knowledge.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: Soft tactile feel is a verified extra fact beyond the no-glare prompt/key. The further «полированную поверхность» claim is unresolved.

defects.ground: Retained Book Textures says only «polished». It does not identify a polishing process or a physically polished surface; the Russian wording commits to that reading of an ambiguous marketing adjective. Soft feel is supported, but does not validate this additional clause.
